title: Skewers
concept: A pin in reverse: the big piece is in front and has to move, then you take what's behind.

glossary.definition: An attack on a valuable piece with another piece lined up behind it. When the front piece moves out of the way, you take the one behind.

summary: When the enemy king or queen lines up with another piece, attack along that line. The big piece must move, and the one behind falls.

narration: White's king steps to e4, right in front of its own queen on e3. King and queen on the same line? Bapu's ears just pricked up.
Rook to e6, check! The king is in front and the queen is right behind it on the same file.
The king has to step off the e-file, and that leaves the queen exposed.
Rook takes the queen. That's a skewer: attack the big piece, take the one behind it.

guided.hint: White's king and rook are on the same file. Can your rook check the king from the other end?
guided.explanation: Rook to d2 is check, and White's rook is hiding behind the king on the d-file. The king steps aside, and the rook falls.

guided.hint: Black's king and bishop share a diagonal. Which bishop move checks the king along it?
guided.explanation: Bishop to e5 is check, with Black's bishop on b8 lined up behind the king. Your king and the f4 pawn guard your bishop, so the king can't take it. Once it steps aside, b8 is yours.

guided.hint: Black's king and bishop are on the same row. Find a rook check along it.
guided.explanation: Rook to h7 is check along the 7th row, and the bishop on c7 sits behind the king. The king steps away, and you take the bishop.
